sources.title: Language Models can Solve Computer Tasks
sources.publication_status: Peer-reviewed conference paper; official proceedings record
sources.content_locator: Official NeurIPS abstract, lines 0-9; Recursive Criticizes and Improves (RCI) claim is abstract-level.

findings.claim: A useful prompt can represent investigation as a small search: state competing candidate explanations or approaches, compare their evidence, then select a next discriminator. Tree of Thoughts formalizes alternative generation, evaluation, lookahead and backtracking; its paper also reports a GPT-3.5 result better than chain-of-thought on two benchmark tasks, but on different tasks than repository research.
findings.support_locator: ToT Sections 1 and 3 (PDF lines 92-108, 165-187); Appendix B.2 compares GPT-3.5 and GPT-4 on Creative Writing/Game of 24, and B.3 reports higher token/cost use (lines 954-984).
findings.decision_implication: Prompt the scout to produce a bounded set of genuinely distinct candidates with evidence for and against each, then name the observation that would discriminate them. Stop when another branch adds no decision value. Keep expert review of the consequential choice.
findings.assumptions: Candidate branches and evaluation criteria can be made concrete from repository facts and the decision question.
findings.applicability_gap: Published tasks are constrained puzzles, not open-ended architecture decisions over unfamiliar repositories. Model quality and extra inference cost vary; ToT itself reports potentially 5-100x generated tokens over CoT depending on task and search design.
findings.next_discriminator: On matched real investigations, compare ordinary mapping with a prompt requiring at most a few alternative hypotheses, source-backed pro/con evidence and one falsifiable discriminator; have an expert score useful alternatives and correctness blind to arm.

findings.claim: Repository investigation benefits from interaction with software artifacts and retrieval/testing tools, while repository benchmarks caution that toy or narrow contexts may not predict realistic work. CodeAgent reports gains on its own repository benchmark from artifact retrieval/implementation/testing; RepoCod reports that retrieval-augmented context beat target-function dependency context and that performance was low on more realistic tasks.
findings.support_locator: CodeAgent abstract (ACL record lines 58-60; proceedings paper PDF abstract) describes five tools and CodAgentBench pass-rate improvements of 2.0-15.8 points. RepoCod abstract lines 58-61 describes benchmark scope, <30% pass@1 for each of ten models, and retrieval result.
findings.decision_implication: Require claims to point to the specific caller/helper/config/test/docs inspected; ask the scout to report contrary callers or evidence and a minimal repository-level check, and distinguish static source predictions from observed command output.
findings.assumptions: The scout has authorized access to the relevant source artifacts and can cite stable paths/locations or command identities.
findings.applicability_gap: These papers evaluate code generation agents and benchmarks, not a Luna scout's architecture research or mixed-model handoff. RepoCod covers Python whole-function generation in 11 projects; CodeAgent's gains are benchmark-specific. Neither validates a particular tool stack or model here.
findings.next_discriminator: Judge paired reports for source accuracy, missed contrary evidence, actionable discriminators and expert rework required on actual repository investigations, holding source access and budgets constant.

findings.claim: Prompt changes should be treated as hypotheses evaluated against downstream outcomes. MIPRO proposes instructions using program/data context and iteratively evaluates them against a metric; it reports improvements in five of seven tested multi-stage LM programs with Llama-3-8B, showing feasibility for one smaller open model while leaving transfer to this research task unestablished.
findings.support_locator: MIPRO abstract, ACL Anthology lines 58-61: program/data-aware proposals, stochastic mini-batch evaluation and reported 5/7 program improvement, up to 13% accuracy.
findings.decision_implication: Keep a control prompt and a specific intervention, use same task/source/tool budget, and judge the output on decision-relevant criteria rather than length or number of citations. Prefer one concise evidence packet with uncertainty, scope and next check.
findings.assumptions: The coordinator can define output-quality criteria and compare paired work products.
findings.applicability_gap: MIPRO optimizes modular LM-program prompts on measured NLP task accuracy; its empirical result does not establish value for open research, source completeness, prompt injection resistance, or heterogeneous agents.
findings.next_discriminator: A small paired comparison on representative existing investigations, scored for factual support, useful alternatives, rejected assumptions, review burden and turnaround, would resolve whether this prompt improves this workflow.

findings.claim: Recursive critique/improvement has been studied and was reported to help computer-task performance, but an agent's self-critique remains an output of that agent and should not be taken as independent verification.
findings.support_locator: NeurIPS 2023 official abstract (lines 7-9) reports Recursive Criticizes and Improves prompting and MiniWoB++ results.
findings.decision_implication: Use critique as a prompt to expose assumptions or seek counterevidence; ground its conclusions in accessible sources/runtime traces and retain separate expert acceptance for design or patch decisions.
findings.assumptions: A later independent reviewer can inspect the cited evidence directly.
findings.applicability_gap: The accessible evidence is abstract-only and pertains to a benchmark of computer tasks, not academic evidence quality or architecture decisions.
findings.next_discriminator: Check whether a critique step increases independently verified counterevidence or reduces reviewer corrections on matched investigations.

rejected_or_redundant: Did not use the OpenReview multi-agent-debate search result as evidence: both direct opens hit a browser challenge, so claims and venue status were not verified from accessible paper content.

Did not use OPRO as evidence: search snippet identified an ICLR 2024 paper but its OpenReview PDF could not be opened. Did not use the Justify Your Prompts article because its ACL Anthology page returned a cache miss.
unresolved: No paper directly tests a Luna-high scout discovering counterintuitive alternatives, checking repository assumptions, or handing compact evidence to a stronger mixed-model architecture reviewer.
The proportionate local test needs matched tasks and an expert rubric; this case researched the question and did not run that prompt comparison.

Prompt-injection boundaries and independent patch acceptance were supplied as task constraints; the reviewed papers do not establish those governance properties. Preserve them as workflow requirements rather than claiming these studies validate them.
stop_reason: Used the maximum 16 logical web operations (6 queries, 10 opens); sufficient relevant primary evidence was found, with access limits recorded.
escalation_ready: For Sol/Astra: the evidence supports trying a bounded prompt that explicitly elicits alternatives, evidence against, and a discriminating check, then evaluates compact reports on matched investigations. It does not establish that this improves Luna performance, justifies automatic prompt optimization, or supports delegation/patch acceptance changes.
